column3: This is VLA Forge. You tell a robot arm what to do in plain words, and it trains a policy for that and saves it as a skill once it's tested.

First, something simple: touch the yellow block. The router checks that the arm can reach it. Then it collects demos in sim and fine-tunes from the closest skill it has. I sped this part up four times.
The whole run took seventy-three seconds. It worked in nineteen of twenty scenes it never trained on, and this is its own rollout.
One rung up is two steps in one prompt. The library already has this chain, so the router just reuses that tile. It measured fifty percent end to end.
If I ask for something the arm can't do, like lifting a block sixty centimeters, it says no and tells me why. The jaws top out at fifty-three.
Every skill lands here as a tile with its success rate and train time. You can test one on fresh scenes or remix it with a new prompt.
In the Robot tab you build the arm itself. Here I swap in a ViperX and lock its wrist roll. Each part comes from a real open-source model.

The WidowX fails one check because its fingers only open twenty-five millimeters. It can still train reach and push, so I make it active. When I ask it to pick up a block, the router refuses and gives the finger width as the reason.
This tile was trained on the ViperX. On five fresh scenes it pushed the block onto the square three times.
Every prompt ends up on the ladder with its tier, how long it took, and the success we measured.
